title: One ResourceBudget scope aggregates explicitly nominated resource rows
stage: foundation complete; engine integration not implemented
API: QuotaAllocator::try_acquire_bytes(size_t) / release_bytes(size_t): paired no-allocation accounting for existing RAII owners
contract: Copies of ONE budget handle share its State, nominated-row total, and original backing identity table. Independent scopes remain independent.
Each local row limit and the nominated shared limit must both admit known requested bytes; rejection rolls back live charges.
Nominated CPU metadata includes scope control storage before State backing allocation and metadata allocator allocate/reallocate/free.
Original aliases/adoption share one same-scope payload charge; no relaxed same_scope or inferred resource/device mapping.
Unattributed private upper bounds and unknown provider memory remain separately reported, outside the explicit nominated total.

actual.scope: Flat nominated-row shared total within ONE copied ResourceBudget scope; independent scopes not associated. Foundation only, no engine wiring.

public_ABI.scope: Actual Windows MSVC x64 before pinned public headers vs current headers; size/alignment only, not a universal ABI guarantee. Old cached lease/SDK objects also linked and executed against refreshed core.

limitations: One shared State over actual explicitly nominated resource rows, not a physical device identity heuristic.
Original backing/lease dedup is exact same-scope only. Independent cache/execution scopes must not be implicitly treated as one aggregate.
Unattributed private bounds and unknown native memory are reported separately and excluded.
CPU system nomination includes control state and metadata allocate/reallocate/free; failed local/shared/backing operations roll back live charges.
Controlled host Completion retirement uses the real existing lifetime attachment; no native GPU error or GPU execution injected.
Windows MSVC x64 before/after public size/alignment equality plus old SDK lease objects linked/run; not universal ABI/platform certification.
Actual engine Tensor/weight/IO allocation source, cache-only local policy and correct move/adoption transfer remain outstanding.

ABI_scope: Windows MSVC x64 before/current size+alignment equal; old cached lease/Completion/SDK objects actually linked and executed with one refreshed resource_budget core TU.
proof_limits: 16 host tests, including 8 new cases; no engine, Model, GPU, native GPU error injection or platform matrix.
The controlled Completion test exercises original accepted-use retention after public Completion/drop; the host-controlled terminal releases the original backing charge.
No per-Model shared physical-device cap is claimed. Engine source allocations and meaningful local cache subset policy still need consistent same-scope wiring.
Tensor move replacement and source-aware charge transfer/adoption must preserve backing-before-charge release and prevent reset gaps or duplicate charging.
The nomination is explicit accounting scope, not authority over driver allocation, other processes, or opaque provider private memory.
